newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South African August trade figures due from Friday.
newsitem.headline: South African August trade figures due from Friday.

text.p: South African August trade figures will not be released before Friday, a South African Revenue Services official said on Wednesday.
Originally officials had said the trade balance might be available as early as Wednesday.
Analaysts polled by Reuters forecast another healthy trade surplus for August, helping towards a sharp reduction in the current account deficit in the second half of the year.
A repeat of July's exceptional surplus of 2.58 billion rand was ruled out, but all economists predicted a surplus above 500 million rand with the consensus at 760 million rand.
Aside from the trade balance, attention will focus this week on August preliminary money supply figures, due at 1500 GMT on Friday.
Economists expect year-on-year M3 growth to increase to a consensus 15.7 percent, mainly due to a low comparative period, after dipping to a preliminary 14.69 percent in July from June's 15.65.
Growth in private sector credit extension, however, is seen slowing marginally in August to 17.9 percent from 18.50 in July.
